## H. The load-bearing empirical question has a published answer, and it cuts both ways

The document's #1 unresolved item is whether an LLM compares stat vectors as reliably as it compares integers, and calls it *"the load-bearing empirical question under the whole no-scalar rule."* It is not unresolved.

- **LISTEN (arXiv 2510.25799, IJCAI-ECAI 2026)** ran essentially the proposed test: human rankings held out as ground truth, against a deterministic equal-weighted z-score scorer, single-call LLM ranking, and chunked LLM comparison. Result: the LLM aggregator **matches or beats the deterministic linear-utility baseline**, and the paper's gain over "naive LLM ranking of all items at once" comes from **decomposing by context size, not by attribute count**.
- **DecompR (arXiv 2605.26878)** is the finding that matters for us and is not in the document: *"Holistic LLM judges conflate utility estimation and utility aggregation, yielding unstable implicit weights… these weight-induced shifts also increase with stakeholder count."* Asking an LLM to rank candidates on many competing criteria produces **weight drift**, and the drift scales with the number of criteria. The fix is to **fix the weights before scoring**, not let the model pick them implicitly.

Two consequences the document needs and does not have:

**The no-scalar rule is a systems claim, not a cognitive one, and the document argues it as if it were cognitive.** The repository rule says *once a number exists, every other system becomes a function of it* — that is about what the **designer** builds. Whether the **agent** can aggregate a vector at play time is a separate question, and the literature says agents do it fine. The synthesis never defends the argument it actually needs.

**The document's own recommended leaderboard is the published worst case.** *"A leaderboard whose entry is a SET rather than a number, a reward curve that pays for the set's composition rather than its total"* is precisely the multi-stakeholder case where DecompR says the aggregator will drift. It is proposed without checking whether an LLM can rank it stably. It cannot, unless the weights are published and fixed — which is the same fix the 乘区 posts make.

The distinction is asserted, not defended.
- **Four itemTree entries carry hybrid labels** — "GENRE_CANON noun, ONE_GAME every implementation" (×3) and "GENRE_CANON noun, PLATFORM_ARTEFACT in practice" — against a brief that required exactly one. Every hybrid label is on a category whose `ourOpportunity` is "this is unclaimed." If the noun is canon and every implementation is one studio, the honest label is ONE_GAME and the novelty claim dies with it.
- **The 阵法 three-gauge claim is 1 of ~3 array systems surveyed.** 修仙家族模拟器2's 阵法 is *"影响练阵的成功率"* — a crafting skill, alongside 炼丹/炼器/制符/御兽. Calling it "the best non-scalar structure in the domain" on a single data point from one of ACS's two array systems is inflation.

The design question becomes "how good was your cast," not "how good is your roll." For an agent, that is the most interesting of the four and the document lists three.

The load-bearing facts are that it is per-boss-parity gated (3 points, thresholds at 25/50/75% HP) and that the *inheritable band* is the legible half. Both are anti-grind structures, and neither is mentioned.
- **No foreign game appears in the itemTree, levelModel or statModel** — despite the document naming WoW and Dark Souls in an unresolved item and conceding they were swept shallowly. ## What I'd do with this

The three highest-value corrections, in order: **(1)** sweep the 乘区/damage-formula domain properly — it is bigger than six of the fourteen itemTree categories combined, it is where the log-crit and the sin-counter and the regime-flip and the panel-lies live, and it is where the cost of "no player scaling" is actually paid; **(2)** sweep turn structure — round caps, turn blocks, initiative computation — because it is the substrate that satisfies the project's own turn-denomination constraint and it is already solved, twice, with published numbers; **(3)** re-audit every "exactly one" negative against a second source method, and adopt the ACS lesson generally, because that method failure has already produced one confirmed false claim and I have reversed five more. The 功德 doubling loop and the 雷劫 permanent-equipment-destruction should be added to the dangerList today; both are in a game the document treats as its strongest source.
